brief: A file organizer as a spatial canvas — documents arranged by topic proximity, not lists or grids

dominant_strengths: Genuinely answers the brief — files cluster by topic with floating category labels rather than defaulting to grid or list.
Colored file-type chips (PDF/JS/CSS/MD) form a recognizable visual taxonomy that aids scanning across the canvas.
Restrained chrome — minimal toolbar, zoom controls bottom-left, minimap bottom-right — keeps focus on the spatial content.
dominant_weaknesses: Cards overlap and occlude metadata (Mobile App Wireframes size, Style System size, Analytics Data size) — destroys legibility, looks like broken layout not intentional stacking.
Cluster boundaries are invisible; 'Design', 'Research', 'Planning' labels float without containing shapes, so proximity grouping reads as accidental rather than semantic.
Massive empty canvas with content packed in upper-left two-thirds wastes spatial real estate and creates an unbalanced composition.
fix_priorities: Resolve card collisions with auto-layout spacing or magnetic snap so no card occludes another's text.
Introduce subtle cluster backgrounds (tinted blobs or dashed hulls) to make topic regions perceivable at a glance.
Rebalance distribution across the canvas or constrain canvas size to the active content bounds.
Strengthen typographic hierarchy between cluster labels and file titles — currently both feel like equal-weight body text.
rationale.norman_balance: Reflective concept is strong and visceral is pleasant, but behavioral usability collapses where overlapping cards block the very metadata users need.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes — it commits to spatial topic-proximity organization, but execution of that proximity (overlaps, missing region cues) undermines the otherwise distinctive idea.
